title: Intrinsic independence and regular functoriality on Elkik fibers
statement: An Elkik pair over a characteristic-zero field $k$ is an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with ideal $I=(\pi)$ generated by a non-zero-divisor, such that the nonregular locus $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ is contained in $V(I)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Write $X_m=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^m)$, $I_m=I\mathcal O_{X_m}$ and $(\widehat X,\widehat I)=(\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I,I\widehat A_I)$ for its thick fibres and completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; $\operatorname{Spf}$ has the open primes and inverse-limit structure sheaf. Let $F$ be a strong desingularization rule on finite disjoint unions of generically reduced finite-type schemes over characteristic-zero fields. Thus $F(X)$ is a finite ordered blowup tower with nonempty coherent regular centers lying over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ and regular terminal scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent]. Assume EXPLICITLY that $F$ is compatible with every regular scheme morphism, including between schemes over different fields: its source tower is the pullback target tower with exactly empty centers deleted and all other extended center ideals retained in order. Regular means flat with geometrically regular fibres [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism]. For a tower $X^{(p)}\to\cdots\to X^{(0)}=X$ and sufficiently large $n>p$, its $n$-th staggered restriction has levels $X^{(i)}_{n(n-i)}$ and the restrictions of the center subschemes, with $I$ extended at each level. These arrows are recorded as centered morphisms, without asserting that unequal-thickness arrows are isomorphisms off their centers. A common-precision restriction of such a diagram means restricting EVERY level to its fibre modulo the $t$-th power of the distinguished ideal; it is defined for $1\leq t\leq n(n-p)$. For Elkik pairs $(X,I)$ and $(Y,J)$ over possibly different characteristic-zero fields, there exists $r\geq0$ depending only on $(X,I)$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ depending on both pairs and $F$, every regular morphism of thick pairs $h:(Y_{n^2+r},J_{n^2+r})\to(X_{n^2+r},I_{n^2+r})$ induces compatible comparisons at common precision as follows. Put $P=\max(p_X,p_Y)$ for the lengths of $F(X)$ and $F(Y)$. At every $1\leq t\leq n(n-P)$ the common-precision restriction of $F(Y)$ is isomorphic to the pullback under $h_t$ of that of $F(X)$ with precisely the empty centers deleted. All retained center subschemes (restricted to precision $t$) and their order are preserved. These isomorphisms, one for each such $t$, can be chosen so that the isomorphism at $t$ restricts to the isomorphism at every smaller $t'$. No uniqueness among ALL automorphisms of a truncated tower is asserted. A morphism of thick pairs means a scheme map with $J_m=I_m\mathcal O_{Y_m}$; it need not lift to a morphism of Elkik pairs or respect their fields. Consequently, for any regular morphism of the completed pairs $(\widehat Y,\widehat J)\to(\widehat X,\widehat I)$ preserving the distinguished ideals, the completed ordered $F$-towers have this same pullback-and-delete-empty compatibility. In particular, when two Elkik pairs have identified completions, their completed ordered towers are uniquely identified over that fixed completion, independently of their algebraizations and fields. The assertions apply as well to finite disjoint unions of Elkik pairs, using $F$ on the whole union to retain the synchronization of stages. On affine charts a regular morphism of completed pairs means a continuous map of their Noetherian complete rings that is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and extends the distinguished ideal exactly. A completed tower is obtained by completing each ordinary blowup along the extended distinguished ideal; a formal blowup is defined by this operation on affine charts.

source.place: Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2, definitions §§3.2.3–3.2.4 and §3.3.1, restrictions §§3.3.4–3.3.7 (Lemmas 3.3.3 and 3.3.4), Proposition 3.3.5 (§3.3.8, printed pp.24–25) including its all-regular-morphisms hypothesis and possibly different fields. proof.text: First work over one fixed field and fix an affine target pair $(T,H)$. Apply [lem-per-elkik-smooth-span-lifting] with its identity smooth map. A smooth thick-pair map at precision $M+r$, with $M>r$, has a span $Y\xleftarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{f}T$ inducing that map at precision $M$, where $f$ is smooth and $g_t$ is an isomorphism for every $t$. By the ASSUMED regular functoriality of $F$, the two pullbacks to $Z$ of $F(Y)$ and $F(T)$ give the same tower after contracting empty centers. The centers of $F(Y)$ all lie over $V(J)$, and $g$ contains that entire fibre, so no nonempty center of $F(Y)$ disappears under $g$. Consequently, reducing every level to a common $t\leq M$ gives an isomorphism from $F(Y)_t$ to the contracted pullback of $F(T)_t$ under the given thick map. The isomorphism at this stage is allowed to depend on the span. The same argument works on finite affine covers of a source open neighborhood of its closed fibre.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.2 and proof of Lemma 3.3.4; compare at equal precision, not unequal ghost arrows

proof.text: Choose the rational model systems of [lem-per-elkik-rational-smooth-models] for $X$ and $Y$, and fix target and source stages $a_0,b_0$. Apply [lem-per-elkik-smooth-span-lifting] to $X_{a_0}$ to obtain $r$. Its UNIFORM clause applies to every later target stage, since the transition to $X_{a_0}$ is smooth. For any $M>r$, a regular $h:Y_{M+r}\to X_{M+r}$ factors after projection to $X_{a_0,M+r}$ through a smooth map $U_{M+r}\to X_{a_0,M+r}$ at a later source stage. Apply step 1 on a finite affine cover of $U$. Pull the resulting comparisons back along the regular source projection. The assumed functoriality of $F$ for the projections identifies the towers on $X$ and $Y$ with the contracted model towers. The source projection lands in $U$ on its whole closed fibre, which is all that any supported center or completed level needs. Thus comparisons at common precision exist without lifting $h$ to a map $Y\to X$. The direction used is $Y\to Y_b\dashrightarrow X_{a_0}$; the printed proof of Proposition 3.3.5 interchanges X and Y in this paragraph.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, proof, printed p.25; corrected direction of finite-stage factorization

proof.text: There is a uniform finite precision loss for all the choices in step 2. Fix the two model towers $F(X_{a_0})$ and $F(Y_{b_0})$. For each center ideal $C_i$, its support lies over the distinguished fibre, hence some power $I^{e_i}$ is contained in $C_i$: on a finite affine cover, take powers killing each generator of $I$ in the center quotient and take their maximum. Take the sum of these finitely many exponents, enlarged to $L\geq1$. Under later smooth model maps or the regular projections, the extended ideals contain the same powers; contraction only removes terms. Two choices of span agree at precision $M$ on the base after identifying their completed source through $g_t$. Their first extended center ideals agree exactly, since their differences lie in $J^M$ and both contain $J^{e_0}$, for $M>e_0$. Apply [lem-per-supported-blowup-precision-loss] to their induced blowup maps: they agree at precision $M-e_0$. Repeat for each center, padding the shorter source tower by empty stages. The next center ideals agree by the same power-containment argument. This proves agreement of the induced tower comparisons at all $t\leq M-L$. The model systems of $X$ and $Y$ and the target stage $a_0$ are fixed once; for two source stages $b,b'$ take a common larger index, and functoriality of $F$ for the smooth transition maps reduces the comparison to this same argument. On overlapping affine opens use a finite affine refinement and this agreement; the resulting maps glue, since their restrictions agree as morphisms of ringed spaces.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.3 chart congruence argument, finite iteration; Proposition 3.3.5 common refinement

proof.text: Take $M=n^2$. All original centers are contained in a fixed finite thickening, since there are only finitely many centers and finite affine covers. Enlarge $n$ so that $n>P$, $n^2>r+L$, and $nP\geq L$ if $P>0$. Then every precision $1\leq t\leq n(n-P)$ is at most $M-L$, so step 3 shows that the common-precision comparisons in the statement do not depend on the span or source stage used. Restricting a comparison to a smaller $t$ gives another construction of that comparison, hence it is the same by step 3. If $P=0$, both diagrams consist only of their bases and $h_t$ itself supplies the pullback identification, with no precision loss. Empty stages are deleted AFTER passing to a common precision: an empty blowup is then an isomorphism. None of this treats the map $A/I^{q}\to A/I^{q-n}$ as an isomorphism. The choice of $n$ depends on the fixed pairs, the fixed model towers and their powers, never on $h$.

source.place: Equal-precision repair of §§3.3.5--3.3.8; elementary inequalities and restriction of the constructed comparisons

proof.text: Let $\widehat h:\widehat Y\to\widehat X$ be regular and preserve the principal ideals. On completed affine rings, reduce the regular map modulo $I^m$. This is a finite-type base change, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] makes the quotient map regular. The quotient identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identify it with $h_m:Y_m\to X_m$. Apply the preceding steps for every sufficiently large $n$. Comparisons coming from different $n$ agree at any fixed $t$ after choosing a larger $n$: both come from the same base map to higher precision, and the precision-loss argument of step 3 applies. The same argument for composite base maps shows composition compatibility. All retained supported centers eventually occur with their entire scheme structure, since their ideals contain a fixed power. Thus the deletion pattern, order and full center ideals stabilize.

source.place: §3.4.1 and Stacks Tag 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change); completion quotients Tag 05GG

proof.text: For each fixed level and every fixed $t$, step 5 has given mutually compatible inverse isomorphisms of its $t$-th fibres, respecting the center ideals. A completed level has the same underlying space as its closed fibre and the inverse-limit structure sheaf. Taking the inverse limit of these sheaf homomorphisms gives inverse maps of the completed ringed spaces; on every stalk they are isomorphisms of local rings. Hence these are formal-scheme isomorphisms, preserve the centers, and identify the ordered completed tower with the contracted pullback. The comparison is unique over a fixed completion as a centered blowup-tower comparison: on a formal blowup chart it must send each center ratio $a/s$ to the prescribed ratio in the source chart, and these ratios topologically generate the completed chart. Equivalently, apply the precision-loss bound with arbitrarily large $M$ to two induced comparisons. For an isomorphism of completions, apply this construction to it and its inverse; composition compatibility makes the tower comparisons inverse. This proves intrinsic independence, including independence of the fields. No uniqueness for arbitrary automorphisms of finite nilpotent fibres is used.

source.place: §3.4.1, inverse-limit definition of formal structure sheaf and uniqueness of induced centered blowup comparisons

proof.text: For finite disjoint unions, use the given rule on the WHOLE union and apply the model construction to the finitely many component pairs. Use the maximum of the finitely many lifting bounds and precision thresholds and the sum of the finite center bounds. Each stage is a disjoint union of its component restrictions; the preceding affine calculations therefore give the comparison of that stage. Delete a stage exactly when its center on the whole source union is empty, that is, when all its component restrictions are empty. This preserves the synchronization and order supplied by $F$ and proves the last clause.
